words.definition: used to express a result: She was so tired that she fell asleep immediately.
used to add extra information: He is not only smart but also kind.
at the moment something happens: Call me as soon as you arrive.
describes past habits or states: I used to live in Tokyo.
used to express preference: I would rather stay home tonight.
used to give advice or a warning: You had better leave early.
cleft sentence for emphasis: It is honesty that matters most.
used to say something is true in all cases: No matter how hard it is, keep going.
on the condition that; provided that: You can stay as long as you behave.
used to introduce a contrast: Even though it rained, we enjoyed the picnic.
used to add an important extra point: She is talented; what is more, she works hard.
something is so obvious it does not need to be said
used to state a requirement: I will help you on condition that you try first.
on the condition that something is true: You may go, provided that you finish your work.
without being affected by a difficulty: In spite of the rain, she went jogging.
used to describe how something seems: He acted as if he knew everything.
shows proportional increase: The more you practice, the better you get.
emphasizes when something first happens: It is not until you lose health that you value it.
because of; as a result of: Owing to the storm, the flight was cancelled.
used to express purpose: She studied hard so that she could pass the exam.
regardless of which alternative is true: Whether or not you agree, the decision is final.
with the intention of doing something: She saves money with a view to buying a house.
because of worry about a possible bad outcome: He spoke quietly for fear of waking the baby.
not at all; the opposite of: The result was far from satisfactory.
only; no more than: She did nothing but complain all day.
deserving effort or attention: This book is worth reading.
to be unable to stop doing something: I cannot help laughing at his jokes.
expected to do something by rule or plan: You are supposed to arrive at 9 a.m.
used to add something even less likely: He can't afford a car, let alone a yacht.
with regard to a particular aspect: In terms of quality, this product is excellent.
as a representative of someone: She accepted the award on behalf of the team.
causing harm or loss to something else: He succeeded at the expense of his health.
without being affected by; despite: Regardless of the cost, we must fix it.
if a particular thing happens: In the event that it rains, the event will be indoor.
to be forced to do something: We had no choice but to cancel the trip.
